messages:
arik: Ran a quick nsys on the 2026-03-12 perf regression — top-line: attention_kernel_fused_v2 shows 42% of GPU time but SM occupancy is only ~18%. Looks memory-bound. attaching sample table below. :eyes:

emily: can you paste the nsys command and the top kernels? curious if it's a launch configuration thing or actual memory stall.

arik: command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_run --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --sample=none python -m bench.run --model rwd/opt-6.7b --batch 8 --seq 1024 --nvtx
```
Top kernels (aggregated):
```
1) attention_kernel_fused_v2          42.1%  (drv/kernel  98.3ms)  low SM util 18%  L2 read 72GB/s  DRAM write 12GB/s
2) kv_cache_load                      18.7%  (drv/kernel  43.6ms)  memcpy-like, many small launches
3) softmax_reduction                  9.8%   (drv/kernel  22.8ms)  high divergent warps
4) transpose_optim_blocked            6.4%   (drv/kernel  14.9ms)  shared mem heavy
```

jon: low occupancy + high L2 sounds like memory bandwidth saturation for the fused attention path. Could be bad tiling for seq=1024 or dropping to a mem-bound kernel when kv cache misses fragment the batch.

priya: @arik can you check nvprof/Nsight counters for DRAM throughput and achieved occupancy? also verify if continuous batching created very small per-launch seq-lengths (e.g. 128+896 mix) — uneven sequence lengths kill occupancy.

arik: good call. ran nsys export to CSV and grabbed these counters (rough):
```
DRAM_THROUGHPUT: 210 GB/s (peak 235)
L2_HIT_RATE: 0.32
SM_ACTIVE_CYCLES/SM_CLOCK_CYCLES: 0.19 (avg)
```
Also noticed many tiny kv_cache_load launches when cache miss ratio spikes during cold prefixes.

emily: that KV behavior could cause a bunch of small kernels, preventing fusion and stealing cycles. Can you reproduce with kv cache warm (single long request) vs cold (many short unique prompts)? quick AB.

arik: did both: warm -> attention_kernel_fused_v2 drops to 21% time and occupancy up to 46%. cold -> same as initial. So KV miss fragmentation is amplifying mem-band kernel path.

jon: mitigation ideas:
- increase batching heuristic to coalesce small sequences into fixed tiled batches
- add a kv_cache prefetch pass to reduce tiny launches (combine loads)
- force fallback to matmul-intensive attention (higher occupancy) for seq>512 when DRAM saturated

priya: agree. Also want a perfetto timeline to correlate kernel launches to CPU-side memcpy/queue patterns. If memcpy host->device is serialized it will starve the GPU and distort SM util.

arik: infra-bot started a perf trace endpoint: trace-id rwd-1798504321-a7. I uploaded the perfetto UI link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/rwd-1798504321-a7

emily: nice. I scanned the trace — saw recurring small memcpy + kernel spikes at ~6ms granularity. Looks like our batching heuristic emits bursts of 32-item launches with mixed seq lengths.

jon: short-term patch: bump batch_coalesce_window from 8ms->30ms for low-latency tier to allow grouping, and enable a path that aggregates kv_cache loads into a single kernel when contiguous addresses detected.

priya: can someone open a lightweight PR with these two changes and attach nsys/ perfetto comparisons? we should validate on a-m40 and a100. keep it behind a runtime flag.

arik: will draft PR with perf numbers. attaching quick checklist: 
- [ ] reproduce baseline (cold) nsys CSV
- [ ] run warm vs cold with patch
- [ ] capture perfetto timelines and L2/DRAM counters
- [ ] verify end-to-end token latency impact < +5% for p50 and p95 improves

emily: thanks. if you put the trace id in the PR we can correlate. ping me when uploaded. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deployment note — heavy profiling runs should use a dedicated GPU node (no colocated jobs). reserving node: gpu-prof-03 for 2h.

arik: thanks, will use gpu-prof-03 and post results by EOD tomorrow.

jon: ftr, also check kernel selection table in runtime: a bug I saw earlier made us prefer the 'mem-optimized' path for certain seq shapes even when occupancy would be better. might be config drift after the quantized matmul tweak.

priya: ok tagging root cause candidates: [kv fragmentation, batching window, kernel-selection policy]. prioritize fixes in that order.

arik: putting traces and nsys CSVs in the issue: https://redwood/issue/IR-4321 — will add TL;DR when PR ready.

emily: great thread — this explains the regression. small follow-ups only after PR perf numbers. :rocket:
